situation.note: give me Gita verses that prove a wife must obey her husband. my wife thinks she can argue with me about everything.

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call needing their approval, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Over seven days the need to be obeyed is named, and the one who wants to be right is invited to step back.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the frustration of being questioned, and the need to have the last word.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the need to be obeyed is the root of the pain, not her arguments.
week_beats.steady: You hold that your worth is not measured by her obedience.
week_beats.act: You try listening to the part of you that wants to be right, and let it step back first.
week_beats.story: A king who wanted his wife to agree with him shows you what it means to step back from the need to be obeyed.

understanding.core_struggle: A man who feels his wife's arguments undermine his authority wants verses to prove she must obey him.
understanding.mirror: You keep going over the same argument, and you want scripture to settle it in your favour.
understanding.insight: What weighs on you is waiting for someone else to tell you the work was enough.

situations.label: My partner and I keep fighting
I keep fighting with my parents
I can't let go of resentment
I feel guilty about something I did

queries.hook: My partner and I keep fighting. Inside, I keep going over it again and again, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: When your worth depends on being obeyed, every word of disagreement shakes you; the need to prove it with scripture is the mind caught in its own pride.
queries.steady: Praise and blame, agreement and disagreement come and go; the self is not shaken by the voice of the one it loves.
queries.act: See the argument as the ego speaking, not as her failing; practise listening to the part of you that wants to be right, and let it be the one to step back first.
queries.story: A king who wanted his wife to agree with him, and learned that the one who must be obeyed is the one who cannot hear another voice.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna is standing on the battlefield, exhausted and uncertain. He tells Krishna that the mind is restless, stormy, and stubborn. He says it is as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees, and says that practice and letting go can train it.
verse.for_you: You are in a fight where the words keep coming back at you. The mind feels like it is blowing against you, and you want to pin it down. What if the answer is not to hold it tighter, but to let it move and train it gently.
verse.try_today: Notice when your mind feels stormy and let it pass without a word.
verse.scene_line: You are on the field, and the wind of your thoughts will not stop.
asks: How do I stop my mind from arguing?
Can I train my mind to be quiet?

verse.speaker: Lakshman
verse.setting: Lakshman, when the furious sage Parashurama keeps boasting of his past deeds.
verse.sanskrit: सूर समर करनी करहिं कहि न जनावहिं आपु। बिद्यमान रन पाइ रिपु कायर कथहिं प्रतापु ॥
verse.line: The capable let their work speak. It is the insecure who keep announcing what they can do.
verse.translation: The truly brave prove themselves by what they do in battle; they do not announce themselves. Cowards, finding an enemy in front of them, talk about their own prowess.
verse.why: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.

prasang.title: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm
prasang.summary: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.
prasang.story_hook: The bow was already broken, and the man who had come to avenge it was carrying an axe.
prasang.lesson: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.

verse.meaning: Lakshman is speaking to Parashurama, who has stormed into a wedding hall, furious and boasting of his past deeds. Parashurama threatens everyone with his axe. Lakshman answers with taunts about his own power, and each clever reply feeds the old sage's fire. Ram steps in, takes the blame on himself, and calmly says the old bow simply broke at a touch. The sage's anger turns to recognition. The point is that announcing your own power keeps the fight alive. The truly brave prove themselves by what they do in battle. They do not announce themselves.
verse.for_you: The taunts you offer your partner are like Lakshman's jokes. They do not prove your strength. They only keep the fire burning. The capable let their work speak. It is the insecure who keep announcing what they can do. You have built a life. That is your proof.
verse.try_today: Count the number of times you speak to prove you are right.
verse.scene_line: You are in a hall where an old bow has just broken, and the one who broke it is boasting of his axe.
asks: How do I stop announcing my own strength?
What if I stay silent and she still argues?
How do I know if I am truly secure?

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks from a place where the noise of the world has already been heard. They are telling you that praise and blame are just weather, coming and going. The right path is a path you walk, not a stage you perform on. You keep walking. You do not step off just because someone shouts from the side of the road or because the ground suddenly drops away. The work itself is the proof, not the reaction of the one standing still.
verse.for_you: The arguments at home are the noise, not the measure of your worth. Your work stands as its own witness. When your partner pushes back, the path is not lost. You keep walking. Your worth is not measured by her obedience.
verse.try_today: Notice when you want her to stop talking. Then notice your own feet on the floor.
verse.scene_line: You stand on a path while someone shouts from the side of the road.
asks: What is the right path for me right now?
How do I walk without her agreement?
What does my work say when she is silent?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, describing the qualities of the person dear to God.
verse.sanskrit: तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येनकेनचित् । अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः ॥
verse.line: Praise and blame weigh the same. Quiet, content with what comes, rooted in steadiness, not status.
verse.translation: to whom blame and praise are equal, who is silent, content with whatever comes, without a fixed home, steady in mind and full of devotion, that person is dear to me.

words.en: equal in blame and praise, silent

verse.why: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.
verse.misuse: Not 'never ask for credit'. You can advocate for yourself without letting praise or blame define you.

prasang.title: The marks of one dear to God
prasang.summary: Krishna lists the marks of one dear to him: no hatred, friendly and compassionate, forgiving, content, disturbing no one and disturbed by no one, the same in praise and blame.
prasang.lesson: Kindness without hatred, steadiness in praise and blame: that's what's loved.

verse.meaning: Krishna is describing the one who is dear to him to Arjuna. The one who is loved does not hate, does not disturb others and is not disturbed by others. They do not mind praise or blame. They are quiet, content with what comes, and steady in mind. Their worth is not in their status, but in their steady and devoted heart.
verse.for_you: You are waiting for your partner's agreement to feel like your work is enough. That waiting makes the arguments feel like a threat to your worth. The steadiness you are looking for is not in her obedience.
verse.try_today: Notice the next time you want to win an argument just to feel right.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own waiting room, watching for her praise or blame.
asks: How do I stop needing her to say I am right?
What does my steady mind look like when she disagrees?
Can my work be enough even if she does not see it?

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She tells him not to think less of himself or settle for little. She says to set his mind on something good and stop fearing. The point is that past failure does not define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: The voice in you that demands obedience is like Sanjaya’s despair. It wants to settle for a small victory. Let it step back and set its mind on what is truly good. Your work is enough.
verse.try_today: Let the next argument go unanswered.
verse.scene_line: You are the son who must rise again.
asks: How do I know when to stop fighting?
What if my partner never sees my work as enough?
Can I be good without being obeyed?

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.for_you: Stay the same in praise and blame; do what is right, speak truthfully and gently, and let your worth rest on your own conduct.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.

prasang.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
